clue.text: A record turnover for somebody in the pop music world

definitions.text: A record turnover for somebody in the pop music world

parts.words: A record turnover for somebody in the pop music world
parts.note: turnover looks like business takings, but a pop fan turning a single over finds the B-side on the reverse

explanation.surface: Someone in the pop industry posts a record-breaking turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record turnover' reads as a sales figure; here it is literally turning a vinyl record over to play its other face.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse face of a vinyl single, usually carrying the lesser track, is reached by turning the disc over.

clue.text: Everything planted in boggy ground toppled over

indicators.note: planted in puts the everything word inside the boggy-ground word

parts.note: a fen is low marshy ground
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything planted in the marsh fell over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toppled over' is the definition, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has toppled has dropped to the ground.

clue.text: A woman is able to make up

indicators.note: to make up means to compose from parts, so the letters of is able are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is capable of putting on make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make up' rearranges IS ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's given name, a form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: Reason to speak about money-raising

indicators.note: about tells us the speak word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to say is to speak

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the money word is read upward, i.e. backwards

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Common sense calls for talk about fundraising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason' is the noun for a sound mind, not a cause; TIN is a British slang word for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of mind, being rational, is reason in the sense of one's wits.

clue.text: Harmonious converse

parts.note: converse reads as a verb, to chat harmoniously, but as a noun it means the opposite, so this is the opposite of harmonious

explanation.surface: Two people chat amicably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converse' looks like talk; it is the noun meaning the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Clashing and jarring is the reverse of being in tune.

clue.text: Can set off for a climb

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of can set are set off in a new order, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a hill walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles the letters of CAN SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upward is a rise or climb, the opposite of a descent.

clue.text: In the main this is not mounted

definitions.text: In the main this is not mounted

parts.words: In the main this is not mounted
parts.note: in the main reads as mostly, but the main is the sea, and this marine creature is a steed nobody rides

explanation.surface: Mostly, this thing is not set in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the ocean, and a fish that is a 'horse' no rider mounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fish with a head shaped like a pony's lives in the sea.

clue.text: No longer ministered to for long

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
to tend is to minister to or care for

explanation.surface: Someone is no longer cared for for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolonged or lengthened things, like a long stay, are drawn out.

clue.text: Allow to bawl out about the French

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the
to rate is to scold or bawl out, as in berate

explanation.surface: Someone lets another shout about the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link meaning concerning; 'rate' is an old verb for telling someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something is to permit or allow it.

clue.text: A girl staying in less is due to svelte appearance

indicators.note: a girl staying in a word sits inside it, so the name goes within the letters of less

parts.note: taken as written
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who stays at home more owes her trim figure to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'svelte appearance' is the definition; 'is due to' merely links it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lean, with no spare fat, gives a slim, svelte look.

clue.text: Irregularly-shaped petals of a delicate colour

indicators.note: irregularly shaped tells us the letters of petals are bent into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Oddly formed flower petals in a soft shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregularly-shaped' rearranges PETALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale, soft tints such as baby pink or powder blue are called by this name.

clue.text: One occasion when 14 doesn't make one cross!

definitions.text: One occasion when 14 doesn't make one cross!

parts.words: One occasion when 14 doesn't make one cross!
parts.note: cross reads as angry, but here it is the X marked on a ballot paper, which a teenager under voting age cannot mark

explanation.surface: A teenager is unusually calm on one occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 14-across is the youngster: someone too young to vote makes no cross on a ballot paper on polling day.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote for representatives is held on polling day, when adult voters put an X beside a candidate.

clue.text: Working man likely to be in a union?

definitions.meaning: a carpenter who makes doors and window frames is a tradesman, a working man

definitions.text: likely to be in a union?
definitions.meaning: one who signs up for things, e.g. a trade union or club

explanation.surface: A labourer is probably a trade union member.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking tradesman bears this name, and so does anyone who signs up as a member of a club or union.

clue.text: Covering of book a king lent getting damaged

indicators.note: getting damaged suggests the letters of book, a king and lent are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: The cover of a book a king lent is getting damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting damaged' rearranges A KING LENT into LANKETING, set after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer that covers something completely, like snow, is a blanket of it.

clue.text: Youngster showing sense after a grant is arranged

indicators.note: after puts the word for sense at the end, following the piece for a grant

parts.note: dole is an allowance or grant handed out, especially unemployment benefit
to sense something is to scent it, as a dog does

explanation.surface: A youngster shows good sense once a grant is arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is arranged' looks like an anagram signal but is surface padding; DOLE is British slang for state benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person not yet an adult.

clue.text: A penman's attributes

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or penman, and the 's is kept as a letter

explanation.surface: The qualities of a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attributes' is a verb, not the noun it seems: A SCRIBE'S read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something to a source is to assign it, as a verb.

clue.text: When minimal rises and falls may be looked for

definitions.text: When minimal rises and falls may be looked for

parts.words: When minimal rises and falls may be looked for
parts.note: rises and falls suggest prices, but they are the sea's ups and downs, smallest at the moon's quarters

explanation.surface: A time when prices barely move.
explanation.walkthrough: The rises and falls are of the sea, at their smallest in the period after the moon's first and last quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest daily range between high and low water occurs at this phase of the moon.

clue.text: Conventional view taken about pictures being put up

indicators.note: taken about means the view word is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the pictures word is raised, read upward and so backwards

parts.note: art means pictures

explanation.surface: A traditional observer looks at paintings being hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conventional' in the slang sense: not unusual or not gay.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means orthodox, not unusual, in slang.

clue.text: Produce notes about tiny number offering bribes

indicators.note: about tells us the singing word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes
wee is Scottish for small or tiny
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone sings about a tiny sum to grease palms.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweetener is slang for a bribe; WEE is Scots for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is a bribe, so making a deal sweeter means offering an inducement.

clue.text: Some candidate sternly rebuked by the examiner

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A candidate is sternly told off by the person conducting the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'rebuked by the examiner' is no definition of the answer: only 'the examiner' defines it, and 'rebuked by' is surface linking.
explanation.definitionFit: One who checks or tries things out, an assessor, is an examiner.

clue.text: A pecan nuts appetiser

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of a pecan are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pecan nut served as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' is the shuffle signal, not more nuts; it rearranges A PECAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A small savoury bite on bread served before a meal is a starter or appetiser.

clue.text: Cut string that's tough

parts.note: to sever is to cut
E is a string on a violin or guitar

explanation.surface: Cutting string that is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the top string of a violin or guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh or demanding conditions are hard, i.e. tough.

clue.text: Recall a peer converting this country's currency

indicators.note: converting signals that the letters of a peer are changed into another order

parts.note: L, for libra, is the symbol of the British pound, the currency of this (British) paper's country

explanation.surface: A lord is summoned back to change British money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converting' shuffles A PEER into REPEA; then L, the pound sign in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a law is to withdraw or call it back.

clue.text: Left always with time to complete purchase

indicators.note: to complete places the time word at the end, finishing off the build

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone takes a long time to finish buying something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' here means grip or mechanical advantage, not a buy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanical advantage or grip, as from a lever, is called purchase.

clue.text: Key-rings for guides

parts.note: B is one of the musical keys
taken as written

explanation.surface: Key-rings serve as guides.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen hides a split: B, a musical key, then RINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead or conduct someone somewhere is to take them along, i.e. escort.

clue.text: The result of strain

parts.note: strain suggests stress, but here it is straining a liquid through a sieve or filter, and the liquid that passes through

explanation.surface: Something comes from stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' reads as tension; it is the act of passing liquid through a filter.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that has passed through a filter is the product of straining.

clue.text: Case made for small area of uncultivated land

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land with heather and gorse

explanation.surface: A case is made for a little patch of wild land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is a cover, as for a sword, not a legal argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting cover for a blade is a scabbard or case.

clue.text: Changing gear, give trouble

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of gear and give are changed into another order

explanation.surface: Changing gear gives a driver trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' shuffles GEAR and GIVE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To distress or wrong someone is to trouble or upset them.
